text: The with statement guarantees setup and cleanup around a block, and you can build your own.
A context manager is any class with two dunder methods: enter and exit.
dunder-enter runs when the block starts — here Timer records the start time.
[chuckle] dunder-exit runs when the block ends, printing how long the work inside took.
So the timing logic wraps neatly around whatever code you put in the with block.
[sniff] The crucial guarantee is that exit runs no matter what — even if an error is raised inside.
This Guard's exit always cleans up, and by returning true, it can even swallow the exception.
[sigh] So the ValueError is caught and suppressed, and the program calmly carries on to survived.
[groan] Context managers are how files, locks, and connections clean themselves up reliably — now you can too.
